reasons: It is a stub meant for copying, not a real tool.

terms.meaning: The part of Express that groups web routes under one address.
One web address and the code that answers requests sent to it.
A file that other parts of the app can load and use.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Router setup and template instructions
sections.what: Creates the router that holds this tool's web routes and explains how to copy the template. The comments say the framework already requires a logged-in user, so this file does not add that check.
sections.why: Likely reason: the template is meant to be copied, so its instructions sit at the top.
sections.watch_out: Routes added here are protected only if the framework's login check is in place, so a new public route needs its own review.

sections.name: get
sections.title: Ping test route
sections.what: Answers a request to the ping address with a fixed success message. It shows that the tool is connected to the app end to end.
sections.why: Likely reason: a simple route confirms that the tool loads correctly.
sections.watch_out: The message describes a folder path that does not match where the file actually lives.

sections.name: tool
sections.title: Tool module export
sections.what: Packages the tool's slug, title and router into the object the app loads. The slug decides the tool's web address.
sections.why: The app needs a standard shape to attach each tool, and this object supplies it.
sections.watch_out: Two tools with the same slug would clash at one web address.

summary: A placeholder tool that shows a new tool module can be added and reached through a web address.
purpose: Gives developers a starting point for building a new tool. It has one test route that answers with a fixed success message.
why: The file's header says it is a template to copy, rename and delete once real tools exist.
how: The file creates a router, adds a route for ping, and packages the router with a name and title as the module the app loads automatically.
inputs: A request to the ping route. The framework adds a login check before this code runs, according to the header comment.
outputs: A JSON reply with ok set to true, the tool name and a message.
risks: The reply message hardcodes a folder path that does not match this file's real location. Copying the template without renaming the slug could make two tools share one address.
debug: If the ping route fails, check that the tool is picked up by the app's automatic loading and that the login check is not rejecting the request. Compare the exported object with the ToolModule type in the types file.
